key_insight: High-throughput DFT/minima-hopping screening found 58 CuI-based ternary compounds that can act as p-type transparent conductors, including 20 intrinsically degenerate semiconductors.
engineering_relevance: The work expands the material design space for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by identifying stable, wide-gap, hole-conducting halide compounds beyond classic oxide TCMs.
method: Searched CuI-based X–Cu–I ternary compounds with the minima hopping method plus density functional theory.
Filtered candidates by thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Revisited chemical modulation of the valence band design rules using the discovered dataset.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 58 candidate p-type TCMs, 49 of them previously unreported, with 20 degenerate semiconductors and an example standout of Cu2FI2 (3.75 eV gap, 0.262 m0 hole effective mass).
watch_item: Predicted performance still needs experimental synthesis and validation, especially for stability, carrier density, and transparency under device-relevant conditions.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
